title: CPRI v8.0 REC link-layer slice: 8b/10b both ways, hyperframe sync (HUNT, ALIGN, SYNC) on the peer's K28.5, L1 inband rate and version negotiation, vendor byte, uplink IQ buffered for the CPU

words.name: CFG0
words.desc: {pointer p[7:4], line rate[3:0]} sent in the L1 inband stream; the rate is negotiated against the peer's (reset 0x2A)

words.name: CFG1
words.desc: bits [3:0]: local protocol version, sent in the L1 inband stream and negotiated (reset 0x04)

words.name: CFG2
words.desc: vendor byte, sent in control word #4 of each hyperframe (reset 0xC9)

words.name: CFG3
words.desc: spare configuration byte, no effect on the link (reset 0)

words.name: CFG4
words.desc: spare configuration byte, no effect on the link (reset 0)

words.name: CFG5
words.desc: spare configuration byte, no effect on the link (reset 0)

words.name: CFG6
words.desc: spare configuration byte, no effect on the link (reset 0)

words.name: CFG7
words.desc: spare configuration byte, no effect on the link (reset 0)

words.name: LINK
words.desc: [1:0] sync state (0 HUNT, 1 ALIGN, 2 SYNC), [2] L1 inband negotiation received, [4:3] hyperframes missed in a row, [11:6] IQ words buffered, [15:12] peer protocol version, [23:16] IQ words dropped with the buffer full (saturates at 255)

words.name: NEG
words.desc: [3:0] negotiated protocol version, [7:4] negotiated line rate (the smaller of ours and the peer's)

words.name: IQ
words.desc: oldest buffered IQ word {I[15:0], Q[15:0]}; reading it pops the word when one is buffered

words.name: VENDOR
words.desc: vendor byte received from the peer

words.name: EVENTS
words.desc: [0] loss of sync, [1] code violation; sticky, write 1 to clear (a violation in the same clock wins)

irqs.name: LINK_EVENT
irqs.desc: EVENTS has a bit set (loss of sync or a code violation); set on every clock until EVENTS is cleared, so clear EVENTS first

notes: rx_sym and tx_sym are the line pins, one 10-bit 8b/10b symbol per PCLK; they pass through unchanged. The transmitter runs from reset: K28.5 and the sync bytes at each hyperframe start, the L1 inband stream, the vendor byte and a fixed IQ pattern.
A hyperframe here is 64 basic frames of 16 bytes (the standard has 256). Two commas one hyperframe apart give SYNC; four hyperframes in a row without the peer's comma give loss of sync.
Core registers take whole words: a write with PSTRB != 4'hF gets PSLVERR and is dropped. Only bits [7:0] of CFG0..CFG7 are stored.
